text: A semantic model isn't just relationships and measures — it's a governed Fabric item in its own right, with an owner, a label, and a permissions tab of its own.
This is a real semantic model's Overview tab — owner, sensitivity label, refresh time, and every table and column already documented, right there before anyone builds a single report against it.

Manage permissions is where the owner grants three real levels: Read, to view content built from the model; Build, to create new reports directly against it; and Reshare, to pass Read access to someone else. This is a separate, deliberate grant — not the same thing as a workspace role.

When someone without Build access wants in, they hit Request access — and the owner has already decided what that looks like: an email straight to them, or written instructions pointing at the real process, like a security group to join.

Governance that travels with the model itself, not bolted on after. Next lesson: governed self-service analytics — how Promoted, Certified, and Master Data badges do the same job at scale, across an entire catalog of items.
